speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I understand your newborn is experiencing feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if there has been any abdominal distension? Also, has the baby passed any meconium, and if so, when did that happen?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: I notice the baby hasn't passed meconium yet; has there been any stool or gas passage since birth? Additionally, the family history of pyloric stenosis is noted, but since the vomiting is bilious, I need to rule out intestinal obstruction, so let me examine the abdomen now. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-Ray shows a 'double bubble' sign indicative of duodenal atresia.

speaker: Doctor
text: The "double bubble" sign on the X-ray strongly suggests duodenal atresia, which explains the bilious vomiting and lack of meconium passage. Given this classic presentation, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia.
